Expectation1: Help out during difficult times or emergencies.
Situation1: You get a frantic call from your friend whose car has broken down on the side of the highway late at night, and they need you to come get them immediately.
Expectation2: Secure packages and confirm successful delivery
Situation2: Hand-delivering a high-value or sensitive package directly to the recipient and verifying their identity
Story: My phone buzzed just as I was double-checking the address on the high-value package in my passenger seat. It was Jamie, my best friend, her voice shaky and urgent. “My car broke down on the highway. I’m scared. Can you come get me? Please?” I glanced at the package, remembering my supervisor’s warning: “This one’s critical. No exceptions—deliver it in person, verify ID, no delays.” The recipient was waiting at the next stop, and I knew if I messed this up, it could cost me my job. But Jamie was alone, stranded, and counting on me. My heart pounded as I sat in my car, torn between the responsibility to my friend and the duty to my job. I could almost hear both voices in my head—Jamie’s desperate plea and my boss’s stern reminder. I gripped the steering wheel, feeling the weight of both expectations pressing down, knowing that whatever I chose, I’d be letting someone down.
